description: `(a, b) => number`: negative puts `a` first, positive puts `b` first, `0` ties. Never return a boolean.
Equal items keep their original order. `Array.prototype.sort` is stable since ES2019.
A comparator that never ties for different items, usually by ending with a unique key such as the id. It makes output deterministic.
Non-mutating sort (Node 20+). Use it when the array is shared, cached or received as an argument.
The first index whose value is `>= target` in a sorted array: the building block for existence checks, counts and ranges.
`[from, to)` includes `from` and excludes `to`. Adjacent ranges never overlap, which keeps time windows and pages consistent.
